title: Transitivity of finite-free counit and evaluation coefficient comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X,V,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $f:V\to X$ separated of finite type, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On ordinary small etale derived categories use $Rf_{*,R}$, $G_R=Ri_R^!$ right adjoint to $i_{*,R}$, and $\omega_R=a_{X,R}^{\times}R$, where $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_{X,R}^{\times}$ is right adjoint to the compact-support functor defined by a fixed compactification [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, lem-exc-closed-ambient, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $H_R(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)$ and $D_RK=H_R(K,\omega_R)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-duality-pairing].

Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, with $B$ finite free over $A$ and $C$ finite free over $B$. For a coefficient map $a:R\to S$ put $T_a=-\otimes_R^LS$. Let $c_a:T_aRf_{*,R}\to Rf_{*,S}T_a$ be the extended inverse-image counit transpose; let $b_a:T_aG_R\to G_ST_a$ be the extended exceptional counit transpose using the inverse closed-direct-image comparison; and let $u_a:T_a\omega_R\to\omega_S$ be the extended structure-morphism compact-support counit transpose. The compact-support comparison is the proper projection comparison composed with open extension by zero. Let $v_a:T_aH_R(K,M)\to H_S(T_aK,T_aM)$ be the transpose of extended evaluation. Set $\beta_a=H_S(1,u_a)\circ v_{a;K,\omega_R}$ for Verdier duality. All these are the specified morphisms, with balanced tensor associators understood.

For each of $c,b,u,v,\beta$, comparison for $A\to C$ equals comparison for $A\to B$ followed by extension to $C$ and comparison for $B\to C$, under $T_{B,C}T_{A,B}\cong T_{A,C}$. For example
$$b_{A,C;M}=b_{B,C;T_{A,B}M}\circ T_{B,C}(b_{A,B;M}),$$
$$v_{A,C;K,M}=v_{B,C;T_{A,B}K,T_{A,B}M}\circ T_{B,C}(v_{A,B;K,M}).$$
These equalities hold for arbitrary unbounded inputs for which the displayed functors are formed, without a constructibility or perfectness assumption. They include the identity-extension equations. They identify the actual transposes: for direct image the common transpose is $T_{A,C}$ of the inverse-image counit; for $b$ it is $T_{A,C}\varepsilon_A\circ c_{A,C}^{-1}$ with $c$ the closed-direct-image comparison; for $u$ it is the analogous compact-support counit; for $v$ it is $T_{A,C}$ of evaluation. Thus all five composition laws are independent of the temporary bases.

proof.text: Write $T_a=T_{A,B}$, $T_b=T_{B,C}$, $T_{ba}=T_{A,C}$. If $(b_i)$ is an $A$-basis of $B$ and $(c_j)$ a $B$-basis of $C$, then $(b_i c_j)_{i,j}$ is an $A$-basis of $C$: expansion first in the $c_j$ and then in the $b_i$ proves spanning and uniqueness. By the finite-free scalar-coordinate theorem, the underlying complex of each scalar extension is a finite direct sum of the original complex. Thus it preserves exact sequences and quasi-isomorphisms, even for unbounded complexes (cycles and boundaries are coordinatewise). The derived change-of-rings theorem computes $T_a$ on a K-flat resolution $P\to K$; since termwise scalar extension preserves this quasi-isomorphism, its canonical comparison identifies $T_aK$ with the termwise scalar extension of $K$, compatibly with the resolution maps. The exact scalar-tower theorem supplies the natural associators $\alpha:T_bT_a\cong T_{ba}$ on the unbounded derived categories, represented by $(m\otimes b')\otimes c\mapsto m\otimes b(b')c$, with inverse $m\otimes c\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes c$, and their unit identifications. Below all equations are transported by these associators; composition is right to left.

proof.text:
Apply the current topos scalar-mate theorem with $h=f$, $R=A,S=B,T=C$ on ordinary small etale topoi, with constant rings and their inverse images. Its adjunctions are explicitly the canonical unbounded derived geometric adjunctions, so its $\gamma$ is the present $c$, with the same extended inverse-image counit. Its scalar associator $\beta_W$ is specified on K-flat representatives by $t\otimes(s\otimes p)\mapsto t b(s)\otimes p$. Under the degree-zero commutative ring-factor symmetry, this is exactly Step 1's $\alpha_W$; the resolution identifications established there are canonical. Thus the stated equality specializes to
$$c_{ba;K}\alpha_{X,Rf_{*,A}K}=Rf_{*,C}(\alpha_{V,K})c_{b;T_aK}T_b(c_{a;K}).$$
This gives $c_{ba}=c_bT_b(c_a)$ with the stipulated associators, not a choice of unrelated scalar isomorphisms. The theorem also intertwines the pullback balancing maps; therefore the common transpose, under those identifications, is $T_{ba}(\varepsilon_{f,A})$. Its statement allows all unbounded inputs and does not require invertibility. The finite-free image-comparison theorem supplies invertibility for these $c$, including $f=i$ and the proper morphism in the fixed compactification. No geometric base-change isomorphism is substituted for this coefficient-change mate.

proof.text: For the fixed structure-morphism compactification write $F_R=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ and let $s_a:T_aF_A\to F_BT_a$ be its specified comparison. Write $e_a:T_aj_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}T_a$. The image-comparison theorem identifies $e_a$ with the termwise extension-by-zero coefficient map: on the open it sends $m\otimes b'$ to itself, and off the open it is zero. The two composites for $a,b$ therefore agree already as maps of sheaves and of complexes, by the balanced formula in Step 1; localization preserves their equality. Thus $e_{ba}=e_b\,T_b(e_a)$ under $\alpha$. By the compact-support definition and the stipulated normalization, $s_a=Rp_{*,B}(e_a)\,c_{p,a;j_{!,A}}$. In $s_bT_b(s_a)$ use naturality of $c_{p,b}$ at $e_a$ to move $T_bRp_{*,B}(e_a)$ past $c_{p,b}$. The remaining two factors are $c_{p,b}T_b(c_{p,a})=c_{p,ba}$ by Step 2; the two open factors are $e_bT_b(e_a)=e_{ba}$. Hence $s_{ba}=s_bT_b(s_a)$. Its inverse is $T_b(s_a^{-1})s_b^{-1}$, with the same associators.

proof.text:
For $i$ abbreviate $F_R=i_{*,R}$ and $G_R=Ri_R^!$, and put $d_a=c_{i,a}^{-1}$. By the definition of adjunction mate, the stipulated counit transpose satisfies $\varepsilon_BF_B(b_a)=T_a(\varepsilon_A)d_a$, naturally in the input. Step 2 gives $d_{ba}=T_b(d_a)d_b$. Transpose $h=b_{b;T_aM}\,T_b(b_{a;M})$ under $F_C\dashv G_C$. With object subscripts suppressed, its transpose is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_CF_C(h)&=T_b(\varepsilon_B)d_bF_C(T_b b_a)\\
&=T_b(\varepsilon_B)T_b(F_Bb_a)d_b\\
&=T_b(T_a(\varepsilon_A)d_a)d_b
 =T_{ba}(\varepsilon_A)d_{ba}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first and third equalities are the two specified counit equations; the second is naturality of $d_b$ at $b_a$. The last equality includes naturality of $\alpha$ at $\varepsilon_A$. This is the defining transpose of $b_{ba;M}$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves their equality. Equivalently this is pasting along coefficient functors in the mate-pasting theorem. It identifies the actual transpose, without an argument from equality after forgetting coefficients.

source.place: Paragraph 3, transposition of the two composite coefficient comparisons; explicit counit/evaluation calculation.

proof.text:
For the structure morphism instead put $F_R=Ra_{X,!,R}^c$, $G_R=a_{X,R}^{\times}$, and $d_a=s_a^{-1}$. Step 3 provides the inverse tower identity. Use the mate definition for these specified adjunctions; its transpose formula needs no scalar-linearity hypothesis or invertibility of the right-adjoint comparison. At an arbitrary coefficient object $N$, denote its right-adjoint mate by $\widetilde u_{a;N}:T_aG_AN\to G_BT_aN$. Transposing $\widetilde u_{b;T_aN}T_b(\widetilde u_{a;N})$ gives, in order,
$$T_b(\varepsilon_B)d_bF_C(T_b\widetilde u_a)
=T_b(\varepsilon_B)T_b(F_B\widetilde u_a)d_b
=T_bT_a(\varepsilon_A)T_b(d_a)d_b
=T_{ba}(\varepsilon_A)d_{ba}.$$
These are the same counit and naturality substitutions as in Step 4, now with the specified compact-support functor. At $N=A$, compose with $G_B(T_aA\cong B)$ to obtain $u_a$; do likewise for $b$ and $ba$. Naturality of $\widetilde u_b$ with respect to $T_aA\cong B$ identifies the two routes. The coefficient-unit identifications compose since $(a'\otimes b')\otimes c\mapsto b(a(a')b')c$ is also their composite multiplication. Thus $u_{ba}=u_bT_b(u_a)$ and its common transpose is exactly the extended compact-support counit, precomposed with $s_{ba}^{-1}$.

proof.text:
Use the normalized derived scalar tensor comparisons of the tensor-data theorem on the constant ring sheaves. The tensor-coherence theorem supplies their tensor-tower and identity equations for the unit-normalized scalar associators of Step 1. These are precisely the hypotheses of the scalar Hom comparison tower theorem. That theorem applies on each ordinary small etale site with $R=A,S=B,V=C$, and its $c^a$ is the present $v_a$: its defining pairing is $T_a(\operatorname{ev})\mu_a^{-1}$, with evaluation in the convention $P\otimes H(P,Q)\to Q$. Consequently
$$H_C(\alpha_K^{-1},\alpha_M)\,v_{b;T_aK,T_aM}\,T_b(v_{a;K,M})=v_{ba;K,M}\,\alpha_{H_A(K,M)}.$$
This is the required equation including all variance and associator factors. The theorem proves equality of the actual evaluation transposes and their identity equations, for arbitrary unbounded inputs; it makes no perfectness assumption.

source.place: Paragraph 3, transposition of the two composite coefficient comparisons; explicit counit/evaluation calculation.

proof.text:
Set $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ and suppress only the associators already fixed. Naturality of the evaluation comparison in its second argument, supplied by the scalar Hom tower theorem, gives
$$v_{b;T_aK,\omega_B}\,T_b(H_B(1,u_a))
=H_C(1,T_bu_a)\,v_{b;T_aK,T_a\omega_A}.$$
Substitute this in the composite of the specified Verdier comparisons:
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{b;T_aK}T_b(\beta_{a;K})
&=H_C(1,u_b)\,v_{b;T_aK,\omega_B}\,T_b(H_B(1,u_a))\,T_b(v_{a;K,\omega_A})\\
&=H_C(1,u_bT_bu_a)\,v_{b;T_aK,T_a\omega_A}\,T_b(v_{a;K,\omega_A})\\
&=H_C(1,u_{ba})\,v_{ba;K,\omega_A}=\beta_{ba;K}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here Step 5 gives the dualizing coefficient factor and Step 6 gives the Hom factor. Thus this law is for the defined $\beta$, rather than an arbitrarily chosen duality isomorphism.

proof.text: For an identity coefficient map, scalar multiplication identifies $T_{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity. Its pullback square is the identity square, so the mate identity law gives the identity $c$. The open coefficient map in Step 3 is the identity termwise, hence $s$ is the identity too. The defining transposes in Steps 4 and 5 reduce to $\varepsilon_A$, whose adjunct is $1$; hence $b$ and $u$ are identities. Step 6 supplies $v_{\mathrm{id}}=1$, and the definition of $\beta$ then gives $\beta_{\mathrm{id}}=1$. All equations were proved by equality under specified adjunction bijections, tensor normalization, or equality of termwise open maps. The bases in Step 1 only verified exactness and availability of the finite-free comparisons; they do not enter these morphisms or equations. Every cited comparison and tensor theorem allows unbounded inputs. This proves the stated independence and domain assertions, including zero objects, empty schemes, and rank-zero coefficient extensions.
